item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with President of Iran Masoud Pezeshkian
item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with President of Iran Masoud Pezeshkian (Turkmenbashi, October 8, 2026) 💬 Vladimir Putin: We met quite recently in Bishkek at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit . Today, we have an opportunity to discuss the development of our relations, the situation in the region and how these processes are unfolding. As for bilateral relations, I would like to note that they are developing positively on the basis of our fundamental Treaty , signed early last year. 📈 Progress in the economic sphere is certainly positive. Trade grew by more than 21% in 2025, and this trend continued in the first seven months of this year. Our humanitarian cooperation , I believe, also sets a good example, with numerous events taking place in both Russia and Iran. 🤝 Overall, our relations are growing stronger . I would ask you to convey my very best wishes to Iran’s Supreme Leader for his well-being and every success. Of course, the most pressing issue today is the situation in the region . We know that Iran is making concrete efforts to end the conflict that broke out in the region through no fault of its own . Iran has once again put forward new proposals to resolve the situation by peaceful means. You know our position, Mr President. For our part, we are ready to do everything in our power to help you resolve this situation . We have an opportunity to discuss all these issues. 🇷🇺 🇮🇷 #RussiaIran

item.title: 🌐 On October 8, the 2nd Global Digital Forum #GDF ) opens at the Mechta venue in Moscow’s Gorky Park.
item.description: 🌐 On October 8, the 2nd Global Digital Forum ( #GDF ) opens at the Mechta venue in Moscow’s Gorky Park. The event is held at the initiative of the Russian Foreign Ministry . Embassy of Russia in Indonesia
:
✍️
Article
by Ambassador of Russia to Indonesia Sergei Tolchenov – “Food and Energy Security Under Threat: The Impact of Ukraine and the West on Developing Countries” – published in
Kumparan
(October 7, 2026)
Key points
:
• Since mid-2026, Ukrainian attacks on Russian and foreign civilian vessels carrying food, fertilisers and energy resources in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea
have significantly increased
, posing risks to established international trade and shipping routes.
• In 2026,
Ukrainian neo-Nazis have carried out 214 acts of terrorism in the Black Sea alone
. By comparison, 12 vessels were targeted in 2025, and just one in each of 2023 and 2024.
• Attempts to disrupt economic ties with Russia, particularly trade in hydrocarbons and agricultural products, could have
serious consequences for global food markets
. Russia accounts for
around 23% of global wheat exports
, while Ukraine’s share stands at
approximately 7% and continues to decline
.
• Ukrainian attacks also target
critical international energy infrastructure
, including facilities supporting gas exports through
TurkStream and Blue Stream
, as well as those of
the Caspian Pipeline Consortium
, which has substantial foreign investment. Such attacks
threaten regional energy security
and
risk aggravating instability in global energy markets
.
• Through these actions, the Zelensky regime seeks
to undermine Russia’s standing as a reliable supplier and transit country for energy resources and food
, while keeping the Ukraine crisis in the international spotlight.
•
Russia’s strikes on vessels carrying weapons and military equipment
intended for attacks on civilian shipping, and on the supporting port and military infrastructure,
are
retaliatory
, with their intensity maintained at the level necessary to achieve the stated objectives.
•
Western European countries continue to support Kiev’s policies
, harbouring the illusion that they can inflict a strategic defeat on Russia both on the battlefield and in the economic sphere.
•
The EU uses the term
“shadow fleet” – a concept
unknown
to international maritime law – as a pretext for interfering with international shipping
. Vessels are inspected and detained on contrived grounds, accused of violating so-called “international” sanctions.
• Western restrictions and efforts to limit Russia’s access to international markets are
undermining global agricultural and energy supplies
and
reflect a broader attempt to reshape international economic relations
to Western countries’ advantage
–
an old colonial policy pursued through
neocolonial methods.
• Food, fertilisers and energy resources supplied by Russia
remain vital to the socioeconomic development and food and energy security
of countries across Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Middle East. Although some supply routes will be redirected,
Russia will not leave the Black Sea
.
• Restoring stability in the Sea of Azov, the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea requires
an end to attacks on civilian vessels and interference with established international trade and shipping routes
.
• Our country continues to work with interested partners
to
ensure the safe and reliable operation
of international energy and logistics infrastructure.

item.title: ⚡️ Comment by the Russian Embassy in the Netherlands for TASS (8 October 2026) On the Unacceptable Remarks by Dutch Minister of Defence D.Yeşilgöz-Zegerius
item.description: ⚡️ 🇷🇺 Comment by the Russian Embassy in the Netherlands for TASS (8 October 2026) On the Unacceptable Remarks by Dutch Minister of Defence D.Yeşilgöz-Zegerius 🔹 The latest public outburst by the Dutch Defence Minister, who has never been known for diplomatic tact or restraint, has this time gone beyond all conceivable bounds of acceptability. 🔹 Legitimate questions arise: Is Ms Yeşilgöz-Zegerius speaking on behalf of the entire Dutch Government? Should her statements be considered as an official declaration of a shift towards direct military confrontation with Russia? 🔹 By publicly branding Russia an "enemy" of the Netherlands, Ms Yeşilgöz-Zegerius has once again demonstrated The Hague's commitment to its destructive course of confrontation. In fact, she has shamelessly revealed her desire to provoke an armed conflict with our country. ❗️ We reiterate: Russia has no aggressive intentions towards Europe in general or the Kingdom of the Netherlands in particular. 🔹 At the same time, no one should be under any illusions: we will not tolerate attempts to address Russia in the language of threats and ultimatums. Any encroachment upon the security and sovereignty of the Russian Federation will be met with an immediate, swift and crushing response. 👉 We expect the Dutch authorities to provide official and unequivocal clarification regarding the belligerent and irresponsible rhetoric of their Defence Minister.

👉
We expect the Dutch authorities to provide official and unequivocal clarification regarding the belligerent and irresponsible rhetoric of their Defence Minister.

(See photo) ☝️ The Regional Delegation of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Russia and Belarus confirmed the strike on the organisation’s property in Donetsk. The ICRC warehouse premises were marked with protective Red Cross emblems in full compliance with international humanitarian law. The Ukrainian side had also received the necessary notifications regarding the warehouse’s location and operations.
